issues.description: The problem statement and the template expect a Developer instance method named attend(course:), but the solution implementation defines this method as participateIn(course:). This creates a direct naming mismatch: students read the requirement for attend(course:) and find a stub called attend in the template, but the reference solution implements the same behavior under a different identifier (participateIn). Additionally, the solution's Client code calls attend(course:), while the Developer implementation is participateIn(course:), making the intended mapping ambiguous and likely to confuse students or cause failures when comparing to the template/tests.
issues.suggested_fix: Align the identifier across artifacts. The least disruptive fix is to rename the solution method participateIn(course:) to attend(course:) (and preserve its implementation and behavior). Ensure any internal calls and the Client code reference attend(course:). Alternatively, if participateIn is preferred, update the problem statement and template to use participateIn(course:) consistently — but prefer matching the current problem/template (attend) to avoid changing student-facing instructions.
